shots.name: Plunger Lane
shots.notes: Auto-launch on the button. The ball merges with the right orbit and gets diverted up to the rollover lanes for the skill shot.

shots.name: Left Standup
shots.notes: Lights Access Jet Bumpers.

shots.name: Left Loop
shots.notes: Spells letters in JOHNNY. Nothing registers unless the ball goes most of the way round and does not come back out the way it went in. Can be lit for extra ball.

shots.name: Left Ramp
shots.notes: Short and shallow enough to backhand comfortably. Carries three of the six red Yakuza Strike triangles.

shots.name: Jet Bumpers
shots.notes: Worth a million each in normal play, eight million each during Riot. The only way out is a narrow gap at the bottom that sends the ball toward the right slingshot.

shots.name: Rollover Lanes
shots.notes: Three lanes above the bumpers. Complete them for a bonus multiplier step; at 5X a completion pays 50 million instead. Move the lit lane with the flippers.

shots.name: Crazy Bob's
shots.notes: Deep sinkhole near the middle of the playfield. A wall blocks it from the left, but the right side is open and wild balls fall in often. Kicks out to the right slingshot or the right flipper.

shots.name: Center Lane
shots.notes: Feeds the upkicker. A software-driven drop target guards it and lowers only when the lane is lit — for Start Mode, a Cyberlock, or an orange arrow. Shootable from either flipper but tight from the left.

shots.name: Diverter Upkicker
shots.notes: The sinkhole in the diverter assembly. It fires the ball straight up to the Data Glove. When you are not meant to be locking, the glove just drops the ball above the rollover lanes.

shots.name: Data Glove
shots.notes: A magnetic crane that runs on two axes near the glass. While you have control, the flipper buttons slide it sideways and the extra buttons push it in and out. You get about seven seconds.

shots.name: The Matrix
shots.notes: A three-by-three grid of sensors in the upper right where balls are locked. Where you drop a ball decides both the award you get and which shots become jackpots.

shots.name: Spinner Lane
shots.notes: An oversized, heavy spinner — plenty of shots hit it and simply stop dead. A clean one carries through to the diverter. Worth 100,000 a spin, or a million when lit.

shots.name: Right Ramp
shots.notes: Makeable from the right flipper, though not as a controlled shot. Carries the other three Yakuza Strike triangles.

shots.name: Right Loop
shots.notes: Spells letters in MNEMONIC. Feeds the same diverter as the spinner lane, so it can be sent to the glove, the rollovers, or out the left loop.

shots.name: Right Standup
shots.notes: One target with two lamps — it takes two hits to relight Mnemonic Recovery, and the first hit does nothing while Recovery is already lit.

shots.name: Left Inlane
shots.notes: Lights Throwing Spears for a timed follow-up shot.

shots.name: Right Inlane
shots.notes: Lights Hit Me, which is a one-shot window at the left loop.

shots.name: Left Outlane
shots.notes: Carries Mnemonic Recovery. A drain down this side with the light flashing gets a fresh ball plunged.

shots.name: Right Outlane
shots.notes: Can be lit for Special from a Matrix mystery award. A genuinely bad place to send the ball.

shots.name: Left Flipper
shots.notes: Small flipper with black rubber. Feeds the spinner lane, right ramp, right loop and Crazy Bob's.

shots.name: Right Flipper
shots.notes: Feeds the left loop, left ramp and the centre lane. The flipper gap is narrow, which offsets the short flippers.

goals.title: Rollover Skill Shot
goals.summary: Every numbered ball and every earned extra ball gets one. The launch sends the ball to the rollover lanes with the middle lane flashing; move the light with the flippers and put the ball through it. It pays 25 million times the number of skill shots you have made, counting the one you just collected.
goals.reward: 25M per skill shot made, plus 5 GB

steps.action: Hit the launch button, then slide the flashing lane under the ball
steps.detail: The launch sends the ball straight to the rollover lanes and is worth 123,570 points on its own before anything else happens. Either flipper button moves the flashing middle lane; a made skill shot does not spot that lane toward the bonus multiplier.

goals.title: Bonus Multiplier
goals.summary: Three rollover lanes, and completing all three steps the multiplier. Once you are already at 5X, a completion pays 50 million flat instead — which turns the top lanes from housekeeping into a real scoring shot.
goals.reward: One multiplier step, or 50M at 5X

steps.action: Move the lights before the ball arrives
steps.detail: The flippers rotate them, so most completions cost you nothing but attention.

steps.action: Take Bonus X and Hold Bonus from the Matrix
steps.detail: Hold Bonus keeps the multiplier as well as the value into the next ball, and is worthless on your last ball.

goals.title: Collect Video Frames
goals.summary: Whenever nothing else is happening, a video frame sits on the display. Shoot either ramp while it is showing and you collect it. Frames are worth four million each at the end of the ball, and somewhere around seven or eight of them lights an extra ball.
goals.reward: 4M each in bonus, extra ball at seven or eight

steps.detail: Frames only appear when no mode, Yakuza Strike, Throwing Spears, Hit Me or combo is running.
Both ramps collect, and both are worth 15 million on their own anyway.

goals.title: Yakuza Strike
goals.summary: Three hits on each ramp lights all six red triangles and starts a countdown from 60 million falling at about a million a second. Every lit shot pays whatever is left on the clock. It bottoms out at 25 million rather than zero, so late shots are still large.
goals.reward: 60M down to a 25M floor, per shot

steps.action: Light three triangles on each ramp
steps.detail: A ramp shot only lights a triangle if that ramp still has one dark.
Every orange arrow shot plus both ramps are live, and each one pays the timer's current value.
It runs during multiball, so lighting the sixth ramp and immediately locking your third ball is how the huge Yakuza scores happen.

goals.title: Throwing Spears
goals.summary: The left inlane lights Spears almost all game. Collect by shooting the right ramp or right loop inside a short window — there is usually time for a second attempt. The awards come in a fixed order and the whole ladder resets every time you drain.
goals.reward: Gigabytes, points, Lite Spinner, Quick Multiball, Hold Bonus, extra ball

steps.detail: The inlane relights itself after the award is taken or the window closes.

steps.action: Cash it on the right side
steps.detail: The right loop works just as well as the ramp.

steps.action: Work the ladder toward the good ones
steps.detail: Lite Spinner takes the spinner from 100,000 to a million a spin, and the very next award on the ladder is Quick Multiball, then Hold Bonus, then an extra ball.

goals.title: Quick Multiball
goals.summary: The fourth Throwing Spears award. A second ball is launched and both ramps pay 50 million jackpots for as often as you can land them. There is no shot to qualify and no goal to finish — it just runs until you are back to one ball.
goals.reward: 50M per ramp, unlimited

steps.action: Work the Spears ladder to the fourth award
steps.detail: Gigabytes, then points, then Lite Spinner, then this.
Fifty million a shot, and the left ramp is backhandable, which makes it the safer of the two to repeat.

goals.title: Hit Me
goals.summary: The right inlane lights the left loop for a single quick shot. It pays 25 million the first time and 45 million the second. The trade-off is real: the left ramp from the same feed sets up a Throwing Spear instead.
goals.reward: 25M, then 45M

steps.detail: You essentially get one shot before the light dies.
A weak loop that comes back out the way it went in does not count.

goals.title: Spell Johnny Mnemonic
goals.summary: The left loop spells JOHNNY, the right loop spells MNEMONIC. Complete both names and every switch on the machine is worth 15 million for 20 seconds — the highest-density scoring in the game if you can find the bumpers.
goals.reward: 15M per switch for 20 seconds

steps.detail: Six clean left loops, and weak ones that fall back out do not count.
Eight letters on this side, so it is the longer half of the job.

steps.action: Get into the bumpers for the frenzy
steps.detail: Twenty seconds of every-switch scoring, and nothing racks switches like the bumper nest.

goals.title: Start Mode
goals.summary: The centre lane is lit for Start Mode from the moment the game begins. The lit mode rotates every couple of seconds, so you pick which one you get by timing the shot. All five have to be played before Power Down opens.
goals.reward: Access to the five modes

steps.action: Shoot the centre lane when the mode you want is up
steps.detail: The guard target only lowers while the lane is lit. The ball rides the upkicker and the glove drops it above the bumper lanes.
Start Mode comes back after each lock you make.

steps.action: Or relight it at Crazy Bob's
steps.detail: If you have made fewer mode starts than locks, Crazy Bob's brings Start Mode back.

goals.title: Upload
goals.summary: The most forgiving mode on the machine. Both loops and both ramps are lit and you can take them in any order for 50, 70, 90 and 110 million. Every shot also banks six gigabytes.
goals.reward: 50M, 70M, 90M, 110M plus 6 GB each

steps.action: Sweep the four shots in whatever order suits
steps.detail: Left loop, left ramp, right ramp and right loop, no sequence required.

steps.action: Keep shooting to reset the clock
steps.detail: Every mode shot puts the timer back up to 15 seconds if it had fallen below that, which makes completion very achievable.

goals.title: Cartoon Hero
goals.summary: The same four shots as Upload and the same 50, 70, 90 and 110 million ladder, but here the order is fixed: left ramp, right loop, right ramp, then left loop. You have to cross the playfield each time.
goals.reward: 50M to 110M, 6 GB per shot

steps.detail: Nothing else is lit until this one is made.
Then the right ramp, then back to the left loop to finish.
Each made shot resets the timer to 15 seconds, so a clean rhythm finishes it comfortably.

goals.title: N.A.S. Riot
goals.summary: The odd one out — a bumper mode rather than a shot mode. Bumpers pay eight million a hit, and the spinner lane and right loop are diverted so they feed the lanes. Complete the rollover lanes during it and you multiply the bumper value as well as the bonus.
goals.reward: 8M per bumper, multiplied by lane completions

steps.action: Feed the top through the spinner lane
steps.detail: During Riot the diverter sends this shot and the right loop up to the lanes.

steps.action: Complete the lanes for the multiplier
steps.detail: This raises the bumper scoring, not just the end-of-ball bonus.

steps.action: Let the ball live in the bumpers
steps.detail: Eight million per hit adds up fast when the ball rattles.

goals.title: Download
goals.summary: Three left loops for 60, 90 and 120 million plus six gigabytes each. Short, high value, and entirely dependent on whether your left loop is reliable off the right flipper.
goals.reward: 60M, 90M, 120M plus 6 GB each

steps.detail: Only clean loops that carry all the way round register.
Each made loop puts 15 seconds back on the clock.

goals.title: N.A.S. Cure
goals.summary: Four centre lane shots for 60, 90, 120 and 150 million. The biggest payout of the five modes and the hardest to complete, because the centre lane is a precise shot and it is very tight from the left flipper.
goals.reward: 60M, 90M, 120M, 150M plus 6 GB each

steps.detail: The guard target drops while the lane is lit for the mode.
The lane is far easier off the right flipper than the left; from the left it is a precision shot.

goals.title: Power Items
goals.summary: Finish any of the five modes and Crazy Bob's lights for a power item worth 200 million. That number alone justifies the shot, but the real reason to collect them is that they buy you time in Power Down.
goals.reward: 200M each, plus a longer Power Down

steps.detail: The sign above Crazy Bob's lights, and it is a plain white lamp that is easy to miss on a poorly maintained machine.

steps.action: Cash it before you start another mode
steps.detail: Two hundred million and one power item banked.

steps.action: Take Light Crazy Bob's from the Matrix
steps.detail: One of the Matrix awards hands you another power item without needing a mode.

goals.title: Cyberlocks and the Data Glove
goals.summary: Locks sit at the centre lane, spinner lane and right loop. Each shot rides the upkicker to the Data Glove, which you then steer for about seven seconds before dropping the ball onto the Matrix. Drop it anywhere else and the locks simply relight.
goals.reward: A Matrix award per lock, and multiball at three

steps.detail: Crazy Bob's tells you where one of the Matrix awards is hiding and lights lock one.

steps.action: Send a ball up to the glove
steps.detail: The centre lane, spinner lane and right loop all feed the upkicker when lock is lit.
Sideways on the flipper buttons, in and out on the extra pair. Seven seconds, then it lets go.

steps.action: Start a mode to light locks two and three
steps.detail: The first lock comes from Crazy Bob's; the rest need a mode start.

goals.title: Read the Matrix Before You Drop
goals.summary: After the first lock the display flips through most of the available awards while the lamps on the physical Matrix flash along with them. The game is showing you exactly which square holds which prize — but only on the playfield, not on the display.
goals.reward: Extra ball, Super Loops, Video Mode, Mystery and more

steps.detail: A normal-play shot here reveals the location of one Matrix award.

steps.action: Watch the grid, not the screen
steps.detail: Keep the display and the Matrix lamps in view at once, and when you see the award you want, note which square lit.

steps.action: Drive the glove to that square
steps.detail: Super Loops makes both loops worth 25 million for the rest of the ball, and 50 million if you collect it a second time in a game.

goals.title: Multiball Jackpots
goals.summary: Three locked balls release and multiball begins with a proper ball saver. Which three shots are lit for jackpots is decided by where you dropped the balls — the column you locked in picks the row of shots you get.
goals.reward: 30M for the first three, then 40M, 50M and up

steps.detail: Left column locks give the left jet lane, spinner lane and left loop. Middle gives the middle jet lane, right ramp and left ramp. Right gives the right jet lane, right loop and Crazy Bob's.
After the opening three jackpots the value rotates between those same shots.
Roughly 30 million for the first three, then 40, then 50, climbing from there.

goals.title: Three in a Row
goals.summary: The single most valuable decision in the game. Lock all three balls in a straight line on the Matrix and every jackpot in the multiball is tripled. You are choosing the drop square anyway, so there is no cost beyond planning.
goals.reward: Tripled jackpots for the whole multiball

steps.action: Commit to a line on the first lock
steps.detail: Decide the row or column before you drop the first ball; correcting later wastes a lock.
Sometimes the awards you can see are worth breaking the line for — an extra ball usually is, Bonus X usually is not.

steps.action: Pick a row of shots you can actually hit
steps.detail: A tripled jackpot on a shot you keep missing is worth less than a single on one you own.

goals.title: Touch-Tone Multiball
goals.summary: A rare Mystery award from the Matrix. Two balls launch, and the job is to land three shots in Crazy Bob's: the first hit fixes the ten-million digit of the jackpot, the second fixes the million digit, the third pays it.
goals.reward: Up to 99M per three-shot cycle

steps.detail: It is only occasionally awarded on later software.
Digits flash randomly on the display, so the value you build is largely luck.

steps.action: Repeat while you still have two balls
steps.detail: No modes and no further locks are available while it runs, so it is worth finishing quickly.

goals.title: Power Down
goals.summary: Play all five modes and Power Down becomes available. All four balls go into play and every white triangle shot pays 400 million — but the game starts switching sections of the playfield off, lights and all, a few seconds at a time.
goals.reward: 400M per white triangle shot

steps.detail: Upload, Cartoon Hero, Riot, Download and N.A.S. Cure, in any order.

steps.action: Bank power items on the way
steps.detail: Arrive with none banked and the shots begin disappearing almost at once, with the whole thing done inside about half a minute. Collected items buy you longer.

steps.action: Shoot the sections that are still alive
steps.detail: Drained balls come back after about five seconds, so keep shooting rather than watching.

goals.title: Mnemonic Recovery
goals.summary: The left outlane ball save. It starts the game lit, and once spent it takes two hits on the right standup to relight. Cheap insurance on a machine whose outlanes are wide open, and the one thing worth spending a shot on early.
goals.reward: A returned ball on a left drain

steps.detail: One target, two lamps. The first hit does nothing at all while Recovery is still lit, so do not waste it.
The returned ball is not diverted, so it comes out of the left loop at speed. Be ready rather than watching the display.
Recovery cannot be relit while Yakuza Strike is running.

achievements.title: Straight Through
achievements.desc: Make the rollover lane skill shot from the launch.

achievements.title: Frame Collector
achievements.desc: Collect enough video frames to light an extra ball.

achievements.title: Six Triangles
achievements.desc: Light all six ramp triangles and start Yakuza Strike.

achievements.title: Spear Ladder
achievements.desc: Work the Throwing Spears awards as far as Quick Multiball.

achievements.title: Say The Name
achievements.desc: Spell JOHNNY and MNEMONIC on the loops to start the frenzy.

achievements.title: Hand On The Glove
achievements.desc: Steer the Data Glove and place a ball on the Matrix.

achievements.title: Three In A Row
achievements.desc: Lock all three balls in a line for tripled jackpots.

achievements.title: Ultimate Hard Drive
achievements.desc: Start multiball and collect all three opening jackpots.

achievements.title: Four Down The Middle
achievements.desc: Complete N.A.S. Cure with four centre lane shots.

achievements.title: Powered Up
achievements.desc: Finish a mode and collect a power item at Crazy Bob's.

achievements.title: Power Down
achievements.desc: Play all five modes and start the four-ball wizard mode.

achievements.title: Cyberpunk
achievements.desc: Bank 320 gigabytes in a single game to take the Cyberpunk slot.

drills.title: Slide The Lane Under The Ball
drills.text: The launch throws the ball straight at the rollover lanes, so the skill shot is made with the flipper buttons, not the plunger. Move the flashing lane onto its path before it arrives, every ball, until you stop watching it happen.

drills.title: Clean Loops Only
drills.text: A loop that dies partway round and comes back out the way it went in spells nothing. Take the left loop off the right flipper and the right loop off the left, full strength, and count only the ones that carry all the way through.

drills.title: Centre Lane From Both Flippers
drills.text: The centre lane is comfortable off the right flipper and a precision shot off the left, and N.A.S. Cure wants it four times running. Alternate the feeds deliberately so a ball that lands on the left does not cost you the mode.

drills.title: Run The Fixed Order
drills.text: Left ramp, right loop, right ramp, left loop — shoot it as one rhythm rather than four separate shots, crossing the playfield each time. Every made shot puts the clock back up, so the mode finishes on tempo and dies on hesitation.

drills.title: Commit The Glove To A Line
drills.text: Pick the row or column before the upkicker fires, then spend the seven seconds driving there instead of exploring the grid. Flipper buttons slide the glove sideways, the extra pair pushes it in and out, and if the time runs short, drop off the Matrix entirely and take the lock back rather than wasting it on a stray cell.
drills.reps: one full multiball build, three locks in line

drills.title: Cash The Spear Window
drills.text: Every left inlane roll opens a short window on the right side — take the right ramp or the right loop immediately instead of settling the ball first. The ladder resets on every drain, so the reps that count are the ones that get deep into it inside a single ball.
drills.reps: as deep into the ladder as one ball allows, 5 balls

actionButton.label: Data Glove Buttons
actionButton.location: an extra button on each side of the cabinet, on top of the usual flipper buttons
actionButton.how: Johnny Mnemonic gives you four cabinet buttons instead of two. The extra pair drives the data glove — the magnet crane floating up near the glass — in and out, while the flipper buttons slide it left and right. Every ball you lock and most of what is worth having on this machine gets placed by hand up there.

uses.when: A ball is kicked up to the glove
uses.what: You get about seven seconds of control. Extra buttons push in and out, flippers slide sideways, then it lets go.

uses.when: Placing a Cyberlock on the Matrix
uses.what: Steer to the cell you want. Awards are reshuffled after every multiball, so read the flashing matrix lamps.
Drive the glove straight to that cell — it is the cheapest extra ball in the game if you spot it in time.
All four buttons steer your square around the display to sweep up dots before the clock runs out.

uses.when: You would rather keep the locks lit
uses.what: Drop the ball anywhere off the Matrix and the lock lights come back on.

howItPlays.objective: Johnny Mnemonic is a fast Williams machine about hand-placing balls with a magnetic Data Glove. Play its five modes to open Power Down, and steer three locks onto the Matrix grid -- ideally in a straight line -- to triple every multiball jackpot.
loop: Shoot the center lane to start a mode; the lit one rotates every few seconds, so time the shot to pick which of the five you get.
Send a ball up the upkicker to the Data Glove, steer the crane with all four buttons, and set it on a Matrix cell to lock -- the cell decides your award and which shots pay jackpots.
Lock three balls, ideally in a line, to start multiball with tripled jackpots.
Spell JOHNNY on the left loop and MNEMONIC on the right to trigger the every-switch frenzy, and light the six ramp triangles for Yakuza Strike.
Roll the left inlane to work the Throwing Spears ladder toward Quick Multiball, and play all five modes to reach Power Down.

lights.name: Rollover Lanes
lights.lit: Three lanes sit above the jet bumpers, and a lit one is a lane still missing from the set -- your job is to move it onto the ball's path before it arrives.
lights.flashing: Off the launch the middle lane flashes as your skill-shot target.

control.effect: either button rotates which lane is lit, sliding it left or right so you can set it beneath whichever lane the ball is heading for
control.when: before the ball reaches the lanes, whether off the launch or dropped in from the glove

lights.then: Line the lit lane up and roll through it. Completing the set steps your bonus multiplier, and once you are at 5X a finished set pays 50M flat rather than stepping further -- grab Hold Bonus from the Matrix to carry the multiplier into the next ball.

lights.name: JOHNNY & MNEMONIC Loops
lights.lit: The left loop spells JOHNNY and the right loop spells MNEMONIC a letter at a time, but only a clean loop carrying the whole way round counts -- a weak one that rolls back out the entrance registers nothing.
lights.then: Finish both names to light a twenty-second frenzy where every switch on the machine pays 15M. Send the ball into the jet bumpers then, because nothing racks up switch hits like the bumper nest.

lights.name: Center Lane Modes
lights.lit: The center lane sits lit for Start Mode from the opening plunge and its guard target drops only while the lane is lit, and the mode on offer cycles every couple of seconds so your timing chooses which one you get.
lights.then: Play Upload, Cartoon Hero, N.A.S. Riot, Download and N.A.S. Cure -- all five open Power Down. Relight Start Mode by locking a ball, or at Crazy Bob's whenever you have started fewer modes than you have made locks.

lights.name: Data Glove & Matrix
lights.lit: When a lock is lit the center lane, spinner lane and right loop each send the ball up the upkicker to the Data Glove, giving you about seven seconds to steer the crane -- flippers sideways, the extra buttons in and out -- before it sets the ball on the three-by-three Matrix.
lights.then: Where you drop the ball fixes both your award and which row of shots turns into jackpots. Lock the first from Crazy Bob's and the next two off mode starts; land all three in a straight line and every jackpot in the coming multiball is tripled.

lights.name: Yakuza Strike Triangles
lights.lit: Each ramp carries three red triangles, and a ramp shot lights one only while that ramp still has a dark triangle left, so all six lit is what arms Yakuza Strike.
lights.then: Starting it drops a 60M timer that bleeds to a 25M floor, and every orange-arrow shot plus both ramps pays whatever is on the clock. It keeps running through multiball, so light the last triangle and immediately lock your third ball for the biggest Yakuza scores.

lights.name: Spears & Hit Me
lights.lit: The left inlane keeps Throwing Spears lit almost all game for a quick cash on the right ramp or right loop, while the right inlane lights Hit Me for a single left-loop shot worth 25M then 45M.
lights.then: Climb the fixed Spears ladder -- gigabytes, points, Lite Spinner, then Quick Multiball, where both ramps pay 50M for as long as you keep two balls alive. The ladder resets on every drain, so push deep on a single ball.

lights.name: Video Frames
lights.lit: Whenever no mode, strike, spear or combo is running, a video frame sits on the display, and either ramp collects the one that is showing.
lights.then: Frames bank 4M apiece at the end of the ball, and once seven or eight are banked, an extra ball lights. The ramps are worth 15M on their own regardless, so the collect is never wasted motion.

howItPlays.laneChangeNote: Either flipper button rotates which of the three top rollover lanes is lit, sliding it under the incoming ball -- off the launch the flashing middle lane is your skill shot. Roll the lit lane to complete the set and step the bonus multiplier; at 5X each completion pays 50M flat.

scoring.text: Take the skill shot by sliding the flashing rollover lane under the launched ball, then arm Mnemonic Recovery with two hits on the right standup for an outlane save. Start spelling the loops and collect video frames between events.

Work the center lane through its modes, light the ramp triangles for Yakuza Strike, and grind the Throwing Spears ladder to Quick Multiball. Bank a power item at Crazy Bob's after each mode to buy time later.

Reach the tripled multiball by locking three balls in a Matrix line, then chase Power Down: play all five modes and every white-triangle shot pays 400M while the game shuts the playfield off in sections. Banked power items are what keep it alive.
